notes: kb/Work PB690 (w61d), owner decision kb/Work R47. The file arm of the §7 determination now holds: a record holding a character above U+00FF written to a file with no converting CODE-SET is refused — '91' on record sequential, relative, indexed and report files, '71' on line sequential — nothing reaches the medium and the record area is unchanged; U+0000-U+00FF are written as the byte of the same value, print lines included (the print-only '?' map is gone). MEASURED on the w61d build: 'A€BC' -> '91' / '71' / relative '91' / indexed '91' / print '91'; 'AéBC' -> '00' and reads back byte 0xE9 (ORD 234) on every organization. Every record write encodes through FileCharacterSet.Medium, a strict ISO/IEC 8859-1 encoding with exception fallbacks. retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Intrinsics/CobolIntrinsics.Text.cs#ByteSub (the symbol is deleted: CONVERT RawBytes and every REDEFINES view now share StorageByte.ImageByte (kb/Work PB547)) retired-witness: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Frontend/Pipeline/CompilationInputs.cs#ReadAllText (CompilationInputs.ReadAllText no longer exists: the bytes of a source or library text become characters in SourceTextDecoder.Decode, read through CompilationInputs.ReadSourceText (kb/Work PB1397))
